items.title: Cards
items.body: Every task, goal, note, event, reminder and link is the same kind of thing: a card with a title, optional details and the tool it lives in. Move a card to another tool and it takes that tool's shape: a task in Taskly, a note in Brainly, an event or reminder in Timely, a goal, task or note in Boardly. Double-click a card, or use its ⋯ Details button, to edit it.

items.title: Getting around
items.body: The tool buttons on the right edge of the screen switch between Taskly, Boardly, Home, Timely and Brainly. A small triangle shows or hides them; on narrow windows they start hidden. On phones they're a tab bar along the bottom. The Sedi logo in the top left always goes back to Home. The menu (two lines, top right) holds your data, AI and account settings. The (?) Help button next to it opens this guide.

items.title: Universal Board
items.body: The Universal Board is a holding area for cards in transit, opened from the dark round button in the top right. Drop cards in, switch tools, then drag them out where they belong. It also has a quick-capture field. It never scrolls: it holds as many cards as fit on screen (at least 3), shown as a count like 4/8.

items.title: Trash and Undo
items.body: Drag any card or folder onto the bin in the bottom-right corner to delete it, or use the × on a card. Every delete shows a message with Undo for a few seconds. Clearing completed tasks and deleting lists can be undone the same way.

items.title: Home
items.body: Home shows a large clock, today's date, the weather, and two short lists: Next up (your top To do task plus today's unfinished Timely items) and Recent activity (the last cards you changed). See all opens the full lists. Click any row to jump to that card.

items.title: Taskly
items.body: Taskly has five columns: To do, In progress, Review, Completed and Backlog. Columns never scroll, on purpose: each holds as many cards as fit, shown as a count like 3/8 in the header. When a column fills up, finish, move or delete something. Cards in Review get a timer that brings them back to your attention. Completed never blocks you; when it overflows, its oldest cards go to the trash (with Undo).

items.title: Boardly
items.body: Boardly is a free-form board for each part of your life, organised as category tabs (Health, Relationships, Work, Chores and Admin to start, up to 10). Place goals, tasks and notes anywhere on the board. Goals open into a SMART template. On phones the board shows as a list.

items.title: Timely
items.body: Timely has two modes. Scheduling has Daily, Weekly and Monthly views and a Reminders board. Planning has Projects (lists of tasks) and Goals (goals broken into milestones and next actions). Timely only looks forward: you can't schedule into the past. Past one-off items move to an archive for 30 days. Today's plan in the Daily view is the same list as Taskly's To do column.

items.title: Brainly
items.body: Brainly holds notes and folders on a free-form canvas, and links, PDFs and files in the My links column on the left. Folders can hold folders. Notes support bold, italic, headings, lists and dictation, and can be opened as a Google Doc. The search box at the top searches Brainly and the rest of Sedi.

items.title: The assistant
items.body: The floating atom (bottom of the screen) is the assistant. Tap it and talk, or press ⌘K (Ctrl K) to type. Ask about anything you've saved, or tell it what to change, like "move passport to in progress" or "remind me to call mom tomorrow at 9am". It always asks before changing anything, and keeps a command history on this device.

items.title: Privacy and on-device AI
items.body: By default, voice starts right away with your browser's speech recognition (in Chrome, Google processes that audio) and switches to private on-device hearing once its one-time download finishes; after that, recordings are wiped as soon as they're turned into text. To never use the browser's recognition, choose Private, on this device in Voice and hearing. Mics in cards and notes use the browser's recognition. The default AI engine runs in your browser, so nothing you type leaves your device. You can optionally add Claude or another AI service with your own key in Other AI services. API keys stay on this device and are never included in Download data.

chunks.heading: Sedi Help Center
chunks.text: Sedi is a calm workspace that runs entirely in your browser: tasks (Taskly), life goals (Boardly), time (Timely) and notes, links and files (Brainly), connected by one card system. There is no account and no server. Your cards stay on this device, and Sedi keeps working offline after your first visit.

chunks.heading: Feature: Cards
chunks.text: Every task, goal, note, event, reminder and link is the same kind of thing: a card with a title, optional details and the tool it lives in. Move a card to another tool and it takes that tool's shape: a task in Taskly, a note in Brainly, an event or reminder in Timely, a goal, task or note in Boardly. Double-click a card, or use its ⋯ Details button, to edit it.

chunks.heading: Feature: Getting around
chunks.text: The tool buttons on the right edge of the screen switch between Taskly, Boardly, Home, Timely and Brainly. A small triangle shows or hides them; on narrow windows they start hidden. On phones they're a tab bar along the bottom. The Sedi logo in the top left always goes back to Home. The menu (two lines, top right) holds your data, AI and account settings. The (?) Help button next to it opens this guide.

chunks.heading: Feature: Universal Board
chunks.text: The Universal Board is a holding area for cards in transit, opened from the dark round button in the top right. Drop cards in, switch tools, then drag them out where they belong. It also has a quick-capture field. It never scrolls: it holds as many cards as fit on screen (at least 3), shown as a count like 4/8.

chunks.heading: Feature: Trash and Undo
chunks.text: Drag any card or folder onto the bin in the bottom-right corner to delete it, or use the × on a card. Every delete shows a message with Undo for a few seconds. Clearing completed tasks and deleting lists can be undone the same way.

chunks.heading: Feature: Home
chunks.text: Home shows a large clock, today's date, the weather, and two short lists: Next up (your top To do task plus today's unfinished Timely items) and Recent activity (the last cards you changed). See all opens the full lists. Click any row to jump to that card.

chunks.heading: Feature: Taskly
chunks.text: Taskly has five columns: To do, In progress, Review, Completed and Backlog. Columns never scroll, on purpose: each holds as many cards as fit, shown as a count like 3/8 in the header. When a column fills up, finish, move or delete something. Cards in Review get a timer that brings them back to your attention. Completed never blocks you; when it overflows, its oldest cards go to the trash (with Undo).

chunks.heading: Feature: Boardly
chunks.text: Boardly is a free-form board for each part of your life, organised as category tabs (Health, Relationships, Work, Chores and Admin to start, up to 10). Place goals, tasks and notes anywhere on the board. Goals open into a SMART template. On phones the board shows as a list.

chunks.heading: Feature: Timely
chunks.text: Timely has two modes. Scheduling has Daily, Weekly and Monthly views and a Reminders board. Planning has Projects (lists of tasks) and Goals (goals broken into milestones and next actions). Timely only looks forward: you can't schedule into the past. Past one-off items move to an archive for 30 days. Today's plan in the Daily view is the same list as Taskly's To do column.

chunks.heading: Feature: Brainly
chunks.text: Brainly holds notes and folders on a free-form canvas, and links, PDFs and files in the My links column on the left. Folders can hold folders. Notes support bold, italic, headings, lists and dictation, and can be opened as a Google Doc. The search box at the top searches Brainly and the rest of Sedi.

chunks.heading: Feature: The assistant
chunks.text: The floating atom (bottom of the screen) is the assistant. Tap it and talk, or press ⌘K (Ctrl K) to type. Ask about anything you've saved, or tell it what to change, like "move passport to in progress" or "remind me to call mom tomorrow at 9am". It always asks before changing anything, and keeps a command history on this device.

chunks.heading: Feature: Privacy and on-device AI
chunks.text: By default, voice starts right away with your browser's speech recognition (in Chrome, Google processes that audio) and switches to private on-device hearing once its one-time download finishes; after that, recordings are wiped as soon as they're turned into text. To never use the browser's recognition, choose Private, on this device in Voice and hearing. Mics in cards and notes use the browser's recognition. The default AI engine runs in your browser, so nothing you type leaves your device. You can optionally add Claude or another AI service with your own key in Other AI services. API keys stay on this device and are never included in Download data.

chunks.heading: How to get help in Sedi
chunks.text:
1. Click **Help** in the top right, next to the menu.
2. Ask how to do something, by typing or with the mic.
3. Follow the highlighted steps. The guide moves on when you click the highlighted control.

chunks.heading: How to switch between tools
chunks.text: 1. Choose **Taskly**, **Boardly**, **Home**, **Timely** or **Brainly** in the tool buttons (right edge, or the bottom bar on phones). If they're hidden, click the small triangle on the right edge first.

chunks.heading: How to show the tool buttons
chunks.text:
1. Click **Show tool buttons**, the small triangle on the right edge of the screen.
2. Choose a tool. Click **Hide tool buttons** to fold them away again.

chunks.heading: How to go back to Home
chunks.text: 1. Click **Sedi home**, the Sedi logo in the top left.

chunks.heading: How to add or create a task
chunks.text:
1. Choose **Taskly** in the tool buttons (right edge, or the bottom bar on phones).
2. Click **Add a task to To do** under the To do header.
3. Type the task into **New task title** and press Enter.

chunks.heading: How to complete a task
chunks.text:
1. Choose **Taskly** in the tool buttons (right edge, or the bottom bar on phones).
2. Click the round check on the left of a To do card, or drag any card into the Completed column.

chunks.heading: How to move a task to another column
chunks.text:
1. Choose **Taskly** in the tool buttons (right edge, or the bottom bar on phones).
2. Drag the card into another column. A full column won't accept it, except Completed.
3. Or double-click the card, change **Column**, and click **Save**.

chunks.heading: How to set a review timer
chunks.text:
Prerequisites: The card is in the Review column.

1. Choose **Taskly** in the tool buttons (right edge, or the bottom bar on phones).
2. Click the timer button on a Review card ("Back in…" or "Set a timer").
3. Choose **1 day**, **3 days**, **1 week** or **2 weeks**, or pick a date under **Come back on**.
4. Tick **Use this as the default** to use it for every new Review card.

chunks.heading: How to clear completed tasks
chunks.text:
1. Choose **Taskly** in the tool buttons (right edge, or the bottom bar on phones).
2. Click **Clear completed** in the Completed column header.
3. Click Undo in the message if you change your mind.

chunks.heading: How to edit a card
chunks.text:
1. Double-click the card, or click its ⋯ Details button in the bottom-right corner.
2. Change the **Title** or the **Description**. The mics next to them let you dictate.
3. Click **Save**.

chunks.heading: How to duplicate a card
chunks.text:
1. Hover the card and click **Duplicate**, or open the card and click **Duplicate** in the editor.
2. A copy called "… copy" appears next to it. Click Undo in the message to remove it.

chunks.heading: How to delete a card
chunks.text:
1. Drag the card onto the **Trash** bin in the bottom-right corner, or click the × on the card.
2. Click Undo in the message if you change your mind.

chunks.heading: How to move a card or task to another tool (Taskly, Boardly, Timely, Brainly)
chunks.text:
1. Double-click the card to open it.
2. Under Move to…, pick a tool tab (Taskly, Boardly, Timely, Brainly or Universal), then the place inside it. The scroll arrows show more places.
3. Click **Save**. The card changes shape to fit its new tool: a task moved to Timely becomes an event, a note moved to Taskly becomes a task.

chunks.heading: How to move a card through the Universal Board
chunks.text:
1. Click **Universal Board**, the dark round button in the top right.
2. Drag a card onto the board.
3. Switch to another tool with the tool buttons on the right edge.
4. Drag the card out of the board and drop it where you want it.

chunks.heading: How to capture something to the Universal Board
chunks.text:
1. Click **Universal Board** in the top right.
2. Type into **Add to Universal Board** and press Enter. The mic next to it lets you dictate.
3. Later, drag the card out into any tool.

chunks.heading: How to move the Universal Board button
chunks.text:
1. Drag **Universal Board**, the dark round button, anywhere on the screen. It remembers where you leave it, and its panel opens toward the side with room.
2. To put it back, drag it toward its usual spot under the top-right corner. A dashed circle shows where; drop it there and it snaps into place.

chunks.heading: How to move the assistant
chunks.text:
Prerequisites: On a computer. On phones the assistant stays above the tab bar.

1. Drag **Talk to Sedi (⌘K to type)**, the atom, anywhere on the screen.
2. To put it back, drag it to the dashed circle at the bottom centre.

chunks.heading: How to put moved buttons back
chunks.text:
1. Click **Open menu** in the top right.
2. Click **Reset button positions**. The assistant and the Universal Board go back to their usual places.

chunks.heading: How to move the help panel
chunks.text:
1. Drag the help panel by its top bar to anywhere on the screen.
2. Double-click the top bar, or drop it on the dashed outline, to put it back.

chunks.heading: How to switch tools while dragging a card
chunks.text:
1. Start dragging a card.
2. Hover the triangle on the right edge to open the tool buttons.
3. Hover a tool for about half a second. It opens, and you can drop the card there.

chunks.heading: How to add a category in Boardly
chunks.text:
1. Choose **Boardly** in the tool buttons (right edge, or the bottom bar on phones).
2. Click **Add category** at the end of the tabs.
3. Type a name and press Enter. You can have up to 10 categories.

chunks.heading: How to rename a category in Boardly
chunks.text:
1. Choose **Boardly** in the tool buttons (right edge, or the bottom bar on phones).
2. Double-click the category's name in the tabs.
3. Type the new name and press Enter.

chunks.heading: How to change a category colour in Boardly
chunks.text:
1. Choose **Boardly** in the tool buttons (right edge, or the bottom bar on phones).
2. Click the coloured dot on the category's tab.
3. Pick one of the 10 colours.

chunks.heading: How to delete a category in Boardly
chunks.text:
1. Choose **Boardly** in the tool buttons (right edge, or the bottom bar on phones).
2. Click the × on the category's tab. The last category can't be deleted.
3. If it has cards, confirm with **Delete**. This also deletes its cards and can't be undone.

chunks.heading: How to add a goal in Boardly
chunks.text:
1. Choose **Boardly** in the tool buttons (right edge, or the bottom bar on phones).
2. Click **New Goal (G)** in the Add toolbar on the left of the board, or press G.
3. Type the goal's title and press Enter.

chunks.heading: How to add a task or note in Boardly
chunks.text:
1. Choose **Boardly** in the tool buttons (right edge, or the bottom bar on phones).
2. Click **New Task (T)** or **New Note (N)** in the Add toolbar, or press T or N.
3. Type the title and press Enter.

chunks.heading: How to fill in a SMART goal
chunks.text:
1. Choose **Boardly** in the tool buttons (right edge, or the bottom bar on phones).
2. Click the ⋯ Details button on a goal.
3. Fill in Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Relevant and Time-bound.
4. Click **Save goal**.

chunks.heading: How to move several cards at once in Boardly
chunks.text:
1. Choose **Boardly** in the tool buttons (right edge, or the bottom bar on phones).
2. Shift-click the cards, or drag a box around them on an empty part of the board.
3. Drag any selected card. The others follow. Press Esc to clear the selection.

chunks.heading: How to file a Boardly card under a different category
chunks.text:
1. Choose **Boardly** in the tool buttons (right edge, or the bottom bar on phones).
2. Drag the card onto another category's tab.

chunks.heading: How to switch Timely views
chunks.text:
1. Choose **Timely** in the tool buttons (right edge, or the bottom bar on phones).
2. Click **Scheduling** for **Daily**, **Weekly**, **Monthly** and **Reminders**, or **Planning** for **Projects** and **Goals**.
3. Use **Previous**, **Next** and **Today** to move through dates.

chunks.heading: How to add something to your day
chunks.text:
1. Choose **Timely** in the tool buttons (right edge, or the bottom bar on phones).
2. Click **Daily**.
3. Click **Task**, **Meeting**, **Appointment** or **Focus** in the action row.
4. Fill in What, Day and an optional Time, then click **Add**.

chunks.heading: How to add a block at a specific time
chunks.text:
1. Choose **Timely** in the tool buttons (right edge, or the bottom bar on phones).
2. Click **Daily**.
3. Hover an empty half hour on the day and click the "Add at…" pill, or click **Add something right now** on the now-line.
4. Type the title. Drag the bottom edge to change its length, or drag the block to move it.

chunks.heading: How to add a routine
chunks.text:
1. Choose **Timely** in the tool buttons (right edge, or the bottom bar on phones).
2. Click **Daily**.
3. Click **Routine** in the action row.
4. Fill in What, choose how it Repeats, pick a Starting day and an optional Time, then click **Add**.

chunks.heading: How to make something repeat
chunks.text:
1. Choose **Timely** in the tool buttons (right edge, or the bottom bar on phones).
2. Hover the item and click **Repeat**.
3. Pick Every day, Every weekday, Every week or Every month, or Custom… for your own rule, then **Save repeat**.

chunks.heading: How to tick off a routine for today
chunks.text:
1. Choose **Timely** in the tool buttons (right edge, or the bottom bar on phones).
2. Click **Done for this day** on the routine. The routine stays; only today is ticked.

chunks.heading: How to add a trip or conference
chunks.text:
1. Choose **Timely** in the tool buttons (right edge, or the bottom bar on phones).
2. Click **Monthly**.
3. Click **Trip** or **Conference**.
4. Fill in Name, From and To, then click **Add trip** or **Add conference**.

chunks.heading: How to add a reminder
chunks.text:
1. Choose **Timely** in the tool buttons (right edge, or the bottom bar on phones).
2. Click **Reminders**.
3. Type into **New reminder** on the blank note.
4. Pick a time: **In 1 hour**, **Tonight**, **Tomorrow 9am**, **Saturday**, or **Date & time** for your own.
5. Click **Pin** or press Enter.

chunks.heading: How to add a reminder by voice
chunks.text:
1. Choose **Timely** in the tool buttons (right edge, or the bottom bar on phones).
2. Click **Reminders**.
3. Click **Say the reminder** and say it, like "call mom tomorrow at 9am".
4. Click **Pin** or press Enter.

chunks.heading: How to send a reminder to Apple Reminders
chunks.text:
Prerequisites: A Mac, iPhone or iPad with the Shortcuts app.

1. Choose **Timely** in the tool buttons (right edge, or the bottom bar on phones).
2. Click **Reminders**.
3. Click **Send to Apple Reminders** on a reminder.
4. The first time, follow the setup steps, then click **Send a test reminder** and **It works, send it**.

chunks.heading: How to set up Apple Reminders
chunks.text:
1. Click **Open menu** in the top right.
2. Click **Apple Reminders**.
3. Follow the steps to add the Sedi Shortcut, then click **Send a test reminder**.

chunks.heading: How to add an event to your calendar
chunks.text:
1. Choose **Timely** in the tool buttons (right edge, or the bottom bar on phones).
2. Hover the item and click **Add to calendar**.
3. Choose **Google Calendar**, or **Apple Calendar or Outlook** to download a calendar file.

chunks.heading: How to plan your week
chunks.text:
1. Choose **Timely** in the tool buttons (right edge, or the bottom bar on phones).
2. Click **Weekly**.
3. Type into **This week's plan** on the right and press Enter.
4. Drag plan items onto days to schedule them.

chunks.heading: How to add to today's plan
chunks.text:
1. Choose **Timely** in the tool buttons (right edge, or the bottom bar on phones).
2. Click **Daily**.
3. Type into **Add to today's plan** and press Enter. It also shows up in Taskly's To do column.

chunks.heading: How to schedule a task today
chunks.text:
1. Choose **Timely** in the tool buttons (right edge, or the bottom bar on phones).
2. Click **Daily**.
3. Click **Schedule it today** on an item in Today's plan, or drag it onto a time on the day.

chunks.heading: How to restore something from the archive
chunks.text:
1. Choose **Timely** in the tool buttons (right edge, or the bottom bar on phones).
2. Click the Archive chip in the toolbar. It only shows when something is archived.
3. Click **Restore to today** on the item.

chunks.heading: How to add a project in Timely
chunks.text:
1. Choose **Timely** in the tool buttons (right edge, or the bottom bar on phones).
2. Click **Planning**, then **Projects**.
3. Click **Add project** and type its name.
4. Click **Add task** under the list to add tasks.

chunks.heading: How to set a goal in Timely
chunks.text:
1. Choose **Timely** in the tool buttons (right edge, or the bottom bar on phones).
2. Click **Planning**, then **Goals**.
3. Click **New goal**.
4. Fill in the Wish, Outcome, Obstacle and if-then Plan, a Deadline and up to three milestones and a next action.
5. Click **Create goal**.

chunks.heading: How to add or create a note
chunks.text:
1. Choose **Brainly** in the tool buttons (right edge, or the bottom bar on phones).
2. Click **Note** at the top.
3. Type a **Note title** and write in **Note body**.
4. Click **Done**. Notes save when you close them.

chunks.heading: How to dictate a note
chunks.text:
1. Choose **Brainly** in the tool buttons (right edge, or the bottom bar on phones).
2. Open a note, or click **Note** for a new one.
3. Click **Dictate** in the note's toolbar and speak. Click it again to stop.

chunks.heading: How to format a note
chunks.text:
1. Choose **Brainly** in the tool buttons (right edge, or the bottom bar on phones).
2. Open a note.
3. Use **Bold**, **Italic**, **Heading** or **Bulleted list** in the toolbar.

chunks.heading: How to make a folder for notes
chunks.text:
1. Choose **Brainly** in the tool buttons (right edge, or the bottom bar on phones).
2. Click **Folder** at the top of the canvas and type its name.
3. Drag notes onto the folder to file them. Drag a folder onto another folder to nest it.

chunks.heading: How to save a link
chunks.text:
1. Choose **Brainly** in the tool buttons (right edge, or the bottom bar on phones).
2. Paste the address into **Paste a link** in the My links column and press Enter.

chunks.heading: How to upload a PDF or file
chunks.text:
1. Choose **Brainly** in the tool buttons (right edge, or the bottom bar on phones).
2. Click **Upload** in the My links column, or drag files onto it.
3. Files up to 25 MB each are saved on this device.

chunks.heading: How to turn a link into a task
chunks.text:
1. Choose **Brainly** in the tool buttons (right edge, or the bottom bar on phones).
2. Click a link or file in My links to preview it.
3. Click **Make a task**. It goes to Taskly's To do column.

chunks.heading: How to search everything
chunks.text:
1. Choose **Brainly** in the tool buttons (right edge, or the bottom bar on phones).
2. Type into **Search everything** at the top.
3. Brainly filters in place. Results from other tools appear under Elsewhere in Sedi; click one to jump to it. Press Esc to clear.

chunks.heading: How to open a note as a Google Doc
chunks.text:
1. Choose **Brainly** in the tool buttons (right edge, or the bottom bar on phones).
2. Open the note.
3. Click **Open as Google Doc**. If your Google account isn't connected, the note is copied so you can paste it into the new doc.

chunks.heading: How to talk to Sedi
chunks.text:
1. Click **Talk to Sedi (⌘K to type)**, the atom at the bottom of the screen.
2. Speak. Sedi answers out loud and listens again. Say "bye" to finish, or tap the circle to interrupt.

chunks.heading: How to type to the assistant
chunks.text:
1. Press ⌘K (Ctrl K on Windows), or open the assistant and click **Type instead**.
2. Type into **Message the assistant** and click **Send**.

chunks.heading: How to change things with the assistant
chunks.text:
1. Click **Talk to Sedi (⌘K to type)**.
2. Say or type a change, like "move passport to in progress", "rename gym to morning run" or "remind me to call mom tomorrow at 9am".
3. Check what it plans to do, then click **Confirm**, or say yes.

chunks.heading: How to see the assistant's command history
chunks.text:
1. Click **Talk to Sedi (⌘K to type)**.
2. Click **More** in the assistant's header.
3. Click **Command history**.

chunks.heading: How to clear the assistant conversation
chunks.text:
1. Click **Talk to Sedi (⌘K to type)**.
2. Click **More** in the assistant's header.
3. Click **Clear conversation**. This also erases the command history. Click Undo in the message if you change your mind.

chunks.heading: How to set up the private voice
chunks.text:
1. Click **Talk to Sedi (⌘K to type)**.
2. Click **Set up private voice**. A one-time download lets Sedi hear you on this device.

chunks.heading: How to change voice settings
chunks.text:
1. Click **Talk to Sedi (⌘K to type)**.
2. Click **More**, then **Voice and hearing…**.
3. Choose how Sedi hears you (on this device, or browser recognition), the accuracy, and the voice it answers with.

chunks.heading: How to remove voice downloads
chunks.text:
1. Click **Talk to Sedi (⌘K to type)**.
2. Click **More**, then **Voice and hearing…**.
3. Click **Remove voice downloads**.

chunks.heading: How to turn on the on-device AI
chunks.text:
Prerequisites: A one-time download of about 500 MB (Light) or 1.2 GB (Full).

1. Click **Open menu** in the top right.
2. Click **On-device AI**.
3. Choose Light or Full, then click **Download and enable**.

chunks.heading: How to remove the on-device AI
chunks.text:
1. Click **Open menu** in the top right.
2. Click **On-device AI**.
3. Click **Turn off and remove download**.

chunks.heading: How to use Claude or another AI engine
chunks.text:
Prerequisites: Your own API key from Anthropic or another service, or Ollama on your Mac.

1. Click **Open menu** in the top right.
2. Click **Other AI services**.
3. Choose Claude or Other engine and enter your key or address.
4. Click **Test**, then **Save**.

chunks.heading: How to remove saved API keys
chunks.text:
1. Click **Open menu** in the top right.
2. Click **Other AI services**.
3. Click **Remove saved keys**.

chunks.heading: How to connect your Google account (optional)

1. Click **Open menu** in the top right.

chunks.heading: How to change the weather location
chunks.text:
1. Choose **Home** in the tool buttons (right edge, or the bottom bar on phones).
2. Click **Weather** under the date.
3. Search a city and pick it, or click **Use my location**.

chunks.heading: How to see what's next
chunks.text:
1. Choose **Home** in the tool buttons (right edge, or the bottom bar on phones).
2. Look at Next up, or click **See all** for the next two weeks.

chunks.heading: How to download your data
chunks.text:
1. Click **Open menu** in the top right.
2. Click **Download data**. Sedi saves everything, files included, as one .json file. API keys are not included.

chunks.heading: How to import data
chunks.text:
1. Click **Open menu** in the top right.
2. Click **Import data** and choose a Sedi .json file.
3. Click **Merge** to add it to your cards, or **Replace** to swap everything for the file.

chunks.heading: How to delete everything and start over
chunks.text:
1. Click **Open menu** in the top right.
2. Click **Clear storage**, then **Continue**.
3. Type ERASE into **Type ERASE to confirm** and click **Erase everything**. This erases all your data on this device and can't be undone, so download your data first.

chunks.heading: Troubleshooting: This column is full. Finish, move or delete a card first. (TASKLY_COLUMN_FULL)
chunks.text:
Taskly columns never scroll, on purpose. Each holds as many cards as fit in your window, shown as a count like 8/8 in the column header. The same limit applies to Today's plan in Timely, which is Taskly's To do column.

Resolution: Complete a task, drag one to another column, park it on the **Universal Board**, or drag it onto the **Trash** bin. A taller window also fits more cards.

chunks.heading: Troubleshooting: The board is full. Route or clear a card first. (UNIVERSAL_FULL)
chunks.text:
The Universal Board holds only as many cards as fit on screen.

Resolution: Open the **Universal Board** and drag cards out into a tool, or drop them on the **Trash** bin.

chunks.heading: Troubleshooting: That file isn't a Sedi export. (IMPORT_NOT_SEDI)
chunks.text:
Import only accepts .json files made by Sedi's Download data.

Resolution: On the device that has your cards, click **Open menu**, then **Download data**, and import that file.

chunks.heading: Troubleshooting: That file isn't valid JSON.
chunks.text:
The file is damaged or isn't a Sedi export.

Resolution: Import the original, unedited file from **Download data**.

chunks.heading: Troubleshooting: Timely only looks forward. Pick today or later. (TIMELY_PAST_DATE)
chunks.text:
Timely is for what's coming up, so items can't be scheduled before today.

Resolution: Pick today or a later date. Past items live in the Archive for 30 days.

chunks.heading: Troubleshooting: The upload limit is 25 MB per file. (UPLOAD_TOO_LARGE)
chunks.text:
Brainly keeps files on this device, up to 25 MB each.

Resolution: Upload a smaller file, or save a link to the file instead with **Paste a link**.

chunks.heading: Troubleshooting: Couldn't save that file on this device. It may be out of space. (STORAGE_FULL)
chunks.text:
Your browser's storage for Sedi is full.

Resolution: Delete large files you no longer need from Brainly, remove voice downloads in Voice and hearing, or remove the on-device AI in the menu.

chunks.heading: Troubleshooting: Microphone access is blocked.
chunks.text:
Your browser isn't allowing Sedi to use the microphone.

Resolution: Allow the microphone for this site in your browser's site settings, then try again.

chunks.heading: Troubleshooting: Voice input isn't supported in this browser.
chunks.text:
This browser can't turn speech into text.

Resolution: Use Chrome or Safari, or type instead.

chunks.heading: Troubleshooting: Not enough browser storage for the private voice.
chunks.text:
The on-device voice needs space for a one-time download.

Resolution: Free up space, or choose Light accuracy in **Voice and hearing…**.

chunks.heading: Troubleshooting: Location is blocked.
chunks.text:
Your browser or computer isn't sharing your location for the weather.

Resolution: Search a city in the **Weather** panel instead, or allow location for your browser (on a Mac, System Settings → Privacy & Security → Location Services).

chunks.heading: Troubleshooting: Couldn't reach Google. Check your connection.
chunks.text:
Google Docs and Drive need an internet connection and your own Google setup.

Resolution: Get online, then click **Open menu**, **Google Docs**, and **Connect**.

chunks.heading: Troubleshooting: Add your Anthropic API key in Menu → Other AI services.
chunks.text:
Claude is selected as the assistant's engine but no key is saved.

Resolution: Click **Open menu**, then **Other AI services**, add your key and click **Save**, or switch back to On-device.

chunks.heading: Glossary
chunks.text:
- **Card** — Any task, goal, note, event, reminder or link. It lives in one tool and changes shape when moved.
- **Taskly** — Tasks in five columns that never scroll: To do, In progress, Review, Completed and Backlog.
- **Boardly** — Free-form boards for each part of your life, with goals, tasks and notes.
- **Timely** — Your time: Daily, Weekly and Monthly views, Reminders, and Projects and Goals for planning.
- **Brainly** — Notes, folders, links, PDFs and files, with search.
- **Home** — The clock, weather, Next up and Recent activity.
- **Universal Board** — The holding area for moving cards between tools.
- **Tool buttons** — The buttons on the right edge that switch tools.
- **Trash** — The bin in the bottom-right corner. Deletes can be undone from the message.
- **Review timer** — When a card in Review comes back to the top of the column.
- **SMART goal** — A goal that is Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Relevant and Time-bound.
- **Routine** — A Timely item that repeats. Ticking a day never deletes it.
- **Part of day** — Morning, Noon, Afternoon, Evening or Night.
- **Today's plan** — The list beside the Daily view. It is Taskly's To do column.
- **Archive** — Where past one-off Timely items wait for 30 days before deleting themselves.
- **My links** — Brainly's column for links, PDFs and files.
- **Assistant** — The atom at the bottom. Talk or type to ask about your

- **Private voice** — On-device speech-to-text. Recordings are wiped after transcription.
- **On-device AI** — Optional. A small AI model that runs in your browser, so the assistant can answer open questions and coach you without sending anything anywhere. Without it, the assistant still finds your cards, says what's next and makes changes you ask for.
- **Other AI services** — Use Claude or another AI service with your own key instead of the on-device AI.

chunks.heading: Your data: where it lives and how to keep it safe
chunks.text:
Sedi has no accounts and no server. Everything you make is stored in this browser on this device, so your browser holds the only copy unless you save a backup.

1. Click **Open menu** in the top right.
2. Click **Your data** to see where it's stored, when you last backed up, and what can erase it.
3. Click **Download a backup** to save everything as one file. **Import a backup** restores it in any browser.

What erases Sedi: clearing "cookies and site data" (Safari: "history and website data") for this site, closing a private or incognito window, or using a different browser, profile or device. Clearing only cached images and files does not. Safari can remove data from sites you haven't opened for about a week, so on a Mac or iPhone add Sedi to your Dock or Home Screen.
